blocks.title: Free oscillations
blocks.text: A body executes free vibrations if it oscillates at its natural frequency without the interference of an external force.

For example, a simple pendulum slightly displaced from its mean position vibrates freely at its natural frequency, which depends only on its length (Fig 14.12, a pendulum swinging from A through B to C). In free oscillations, with no resistive force, the total energy of the body stays constant and so the amplitude stays constant.

blocks.alt: A simple pendulum hung from a point O. The bob is shown at the extreme position A, the mean position B and the other extreme position C, with a dashed arc and arrows showing it swinging A to B to C and back. A panel says it oscillates at its natural frequency f = (1/2 pi) square root of (g/l) with no external force, and with no resistance its amplitude stays constant.
blocks.caption: Free oscillation of a simple pendulum (original diagram after Fig 14.12).
blocks.long_description: Once displaced and released, nothing outside acts on the pendulum except gravity and the string, so it swings at its own natural frequency, which depends only on its length (for a given g). Without air resistance its energy, and so its amplitude, would not change.

blocks.title: Forced oscillations
blocks.text: If a freely oscillating system is acted on by an external periodic force, forced vibrations take place, for example when a swing is pushed repeatedly (Fig 14.13).
The vibrations of a factory floor caused by heavy machinery are an example of forced vibrations. Another example is the loud sound produced by the wooden boards of string instruments.

blocks.alt: Left: a swing on its frame, shown at both ends of its swing, with a red arrow marking a push F given at one end. Right: a graph of the swing's displacement against time, a steady wave, with a short red bar under each cycle marking one push per swing.
blocks.caption: Forced oscillation: a swing pushed once in every swing (original diagram after Fig 14.13).
blocks.long_description: A periodic external force (the driving force) keeps the swing going; the swing then vibrates at the frequency of the pushes, the driving frequency, not necessarily its natural frequency.

blocks.title: Interesting information
blocks.text: A guitar string, a ringing bell, atomic oscillations, bridge vibrations and the sway of a building are examples of free oscillations.
